endpoints.name: Activities
endpoints.description: The scheduled work against deals and contacts -- calls, meetings, tasks, deadlines and emails -- one row each. Carries type, subject, due_date and due_time, duration, the DONE flag, add_time and marked_as_done_time, the owning user, and the deal, person and organization it is attached to. The activity-versus-outcome table: done tells completion, due_date against marked_as_done_time tells punctuality, and an activity with no done marker and a past due date is overdue rather than absent. Filter by any of its parent ids, by done, and incrementally with updated_since.

endpoints.name: Activity
endpoints.description: One activity by id.

endpoints.name: Activity Fields
endpoints.description: Every field an activity can carry, standard and custom, with key, name and type. The decoder for hash-keyed custom fields on activities, as Deal Fields is for deals.

endpoints.name: Activity Types
endpoints.description: The activity types configured on the account -- call, meeting, task, deadline, email, lunch and any custom ones -- with name, key_string, icon and order. Activities carry a type key, so this is what turns it into a readable label; custom types make the set account-specific, so it cannot be assumed.

endpoints.name: Currencies
endpoints.description: The currencies Pipedrive supports, with code, name, symbol, decimal places and whether each is a custom currency. Small reference table, and a necessary one: deal, product and goal values are each stored in their own currency with no conversion anywhere in the API, so any total spanning currencies has to be built deliberately rather than summed.

endpoints.name: Deals
endpoints.suffix: /api/v2/deals?owner_id={Owner ID?}&filter_id={Filter ID?}&person_id={Person ID?}&org_id={Organization ID?}&pipeline_id={Pipeline ID?}&stage_id={Stage ID?}&status={Status?:open|won|lost|deleted}&updated_since={Updated Since?:yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ}&updated_until={Updated Until?:yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ}&custom_fields={Custom Field Keys?:key1,key2,... (max 15)}&sort_by={Sort By?:id|update_time|add_time}&sort_direction={Sort Direction?:asc|desc}
endpoints.description: The sales opportunities on the account, one row each -- the central table of a Pipedrive CRM. Carries title, value and currency, STATUS, the pipeline and stage, the person and organization, the owner, add_time and update_time, expected_close_date, close_time, won_time, lost_time and lost_reason. THE STATUS COLUMN HAS FOUR VALUES: open, won, lost and DELETED. Deleted deals are still returned, so any total that does not filter status counts records the business considers gone -- and a win rate is won over won plus lost, never over all rows. CUSTOM FIELDS ARE NOT RETURNED BY DEFAULT: v2 keeps them in a custom_fields object and only includes the keys named in the custom_fields parameter, up to fifteen at a time -- so their absence is an unmade request rather than empty data, and Deal Fields is what supplies the 40-character keys to ask for. Filter incrementally with updated_since and updated_until.

endpoints.name: Deal Search
endpoints.description: Deals matching a search term across title, notes and custom fields. Returns matches with a relevance score rather than the full deal record, so it locates deals rather than reporting on them. Narrow with person_id, organization_id or status.

endpoints.name: Deal Summary
endpoints.description: Aggregate totals across deals -- count and value, broken down by currency and by status, optionally scoped to a filter, user or stage. A ready-made roll-up: it answers 'how much is in the pipeline' without paging a single deal, and it splits by currency, which matters because deal values are stored in their own currencies and cannot be summed directly.

endpoints.name: Deal Timeline
endpoints.suffix: /v1/deals/timeline?start_date={Start Date:YYYY-MM-DD}?interval={Interval:day|week|...}&amount={Amount}&field_key={Field Key}&user_id={User ID?}&pipeline_id={Pipeline ID?}&filter_id={Filter ID?}&exclude_deals={Exclude Deals?:0|1}&totals_convert_currency={Totals Convert Currency?}
endpoints.description: Deals grouped into time periods -- by day, week, month or quarter -- with the count and total value opened in each, and separate totals for won and lost. The trend table: it answers how the pipeline moved over time, which Deals itself can only give by aggregating every row. Choose the field the periods are cut on (add_time, close_time and so on), since the same deals produce a different picture depending on which date is used.

endpoints.name: Deal
endpoints.description: One deal by id. Same fields as Deals, and the same custom_fields rule -- name the keys wanted or none arrive.

endpoints.name: Deal Activities
endpoints.description: The activities linked to one deal. Requires a deal id. NOTE THE SHAPE: v2 replaced the per-deal listing with a deal_id filter on the activities collection, so this is the activities endpoint scoped to one deal rather than a separate resource -- and every activity filter, including done and the update-time range, is available on it.

endpoints.name: Deal Files
endpoints.description: The files attached to one deal, with name, type, size and who added them. Requires a deal id.

endpoints.name: Deal Updates
endpoints.description: The change history of one deal: every field that changed, with its old and new value, who changed it and when. Requires a deal id. The deal record carries only its CURRENT stage and status -- this is the only source for when it entered a stage, how long it sat there, and how often its value was revised. Note the feed also carries notes, activities and file additions, so filter by change type before treating it as a field-change log.

endpoints.name: Deal Followers
endpoints.description: The users following one deal. Requires a deal id. Internal interest, not customer involvement.

endpoints.name: Deal Mail Messages
endpoints.description: The email correspondence linked to one deal, with subject, sender, recipients and timestamps. Requires a deal id. Where email sync is enabled this is the record of actual customer contact, which activities alone do not capture.

endpoints.name: Deal Participants
endpoints.description: The people involved in one deal beyond its primary contact. Requires a deal id. A deal has one person_id but often several real participants, so this is the honest answer to who was involved.

endpoints.name: Deal Permitted Users
endpoints.description: The users allowed to see one deal. Requires a deal id. Visibility configuration, and the explanation for why two people counting the same pipeline get different totals.

endpoints.name: Deal People
endpoints.description: The people linked to one deal. Requires a deal id. The persons collection filtered by deal_id, for the same reason.

endpoints.name: Deal Products
endpoints.description: The products attached to one deal, with quantity, item price, discount and the resulting sum. Requires a deal id. A deal's value is a single number; what makes it up is only here.

endpoints.name: Deal Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a deal can carry, standard and custom, with the field KEY, its human name, field_type, and for enum and set fields the option list with each option's id and label. THE KEY TO DEAL DATA. Pipedrive names custom fields with a 40-character hash, and deals return values under those hashes with nothing else to identify them -- so a column of hashes is unreadable without this table, and single-select values are option ids that only the options list here resolves.

endpoints.name: Deal Field
endpoints.description: One deal field by id, with its options.

endpoints.name: Files
endpoints.description: Every file uploaded to the account, with name, type, size, who added it, and the deal, person, organization, product or activity it is attached to. Metadata only -- the contents are a separate download. Useful for storage review and for finding which records carry supporting documents.

endpoints.name: File
endpoints.description: One file's metadata by id.

endpoints.name: Filters
endpoints.description: The saved filters on the account, each with its name, the item type it applies to (deals, persons, organizations, products or activities), its owner, and the conditions defining it. Filters are the queries the organisation has already agreed on -- 'my open deals', 'stale leads' -- and most listing endpoints accept a filter_id, so these are reusable definitions rather than just UI state. Reading the conditions is usually faster than guessing at what a business term means.

endpoints.name: Filter Helpers
endpoints.description: The fields, operators and value types filters can be built from. Reference data for constructing or interpreting a filter's conditions.

endpoints.name: Filter
endpoints.description: One filter by id, with its full condition tree. The conditions are the filter's real meaning; the name rarely states them.

endpoints.name: Global Messages
endpoints.description: Announcement messages shown to the user in the Pipedrive interface. REMOVED: absent from Pipedrive's current API description, and product announcements rather than CRM data in any case.

endpoints.name: Goals
endpoints.suffix: /v1/goals/find?type.name={Type Name?}&title={Title?}&is_active={Is Active?}&assignee.id={Assignee ID?}&assignee.type={Assignee Type?:person|company|term}&expected_outcome.target={Expected Outcome Target?}&expected_outcome.tracking_metric={Expected Outcome Tracking Metric?:quantity|sum}
endpoints.description: The sales targets set on the account, each with what is being measured (deals won, deals progressed, activities completed or revenue), the target value, the period it covers, its interval, and whether it is assigned to a user, a team or the whole company. Targets stated by the business rather than derived from the data -- so this is what turns a number into 'ahead' or 'behind', which no deal table can say on its own. Progress against them is in Goal Result.

endpoints.name: Goal Result
endpoints.description: The progress of one goal: the achieved value against the target for each period in its range. Requires a goal id and a date range. Pipedrive computes this, so attainment does not have to be reconstructed from the deals.

endpoints.name: Mail Message
endpoints.description: One mail message by id, with its full body and headers.

endpoints.name: Mail Threads
endpoints.description: The email conversations synced into the account, one thread each, with subject, participants, message count, and the deal or contact they are linked to. Requires a folder such as inbox, drafts or sent. Depends on email sync being enabled for the user; without it these tables are empty, which is not the same as no email having been exchanged.

endpoints.name: Mail Thread
endpoints.description: One mail thread by id, with its participants and linkage.

endpoints.name: Mail Thread Messages
endpoints.description: The individual messages within one thread, with sender, recipients, subject, body and timestamp. Requires a thread id. The message-level detail behind the thread summary.

endpoints.name: Notes
endpoints.suffix: /v1/notes?user_id={User ID?}&deal_id={Deal ID?}&person_id={Person ID?}&org_id={Organization ID?}&start_date={Start Date?:YYYY-MM-DD}&end_date={End Date?:YYYY-MM-DD}
endpoints.description: The free-text notes written against deals, contacts, organizations and leads, one row each. Carries the content, the author, add_time and update_time, and the deal, person, organization or lead it is attached to. The qualitative record alongside the structured one -- why a deal was lost is usually written here and nowhere else. Filter by the parent id or by date; the content is HTML, not plain text.

endpoints.name: Note
endpoints.description: One note by id.

endpoints.name: Note Fields
endpoints.description: The fields a note can carry. A small reference list; notes have few fields and no custom ones in the way deals do.

endpoints.name: Organization Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a company can carry, standard and custom, with key, name, type and option lists. The decoder for the hash-keyed custom fields on organizations.

endpoints.name: Organization Field
endpoints.description: One organization field by id, with its options.

endpoints.name: Organizations
endpoints.description: The companies on the account, one row each. Carries name, the owning user, add_time and update_time, and running counts of people, open, won, lost and closed deals, and activities. The account-level dimension: deals and contacts both reference an org_id, so this is what per-customer analysis groups by. Custom fields follow the v2 rule and are decoded by Organization Fields.

endpoints.name: Organization Search
endpoints.description: Companies matching a search term across name, address and custom fields. Returns scored matches.

endpoints.name: Organization
endpoints.description: One company by id. Same custom_fields rule.

endpoints.name: Organization Activities
endpoints.description: The activities linked to one company. Requires an organization id. The activities collection filtered by org_id.

endpoints.name: Organization Deals
endpoints.description: The deals linked to one company. Requires an organization id. The deals collection filtered by org_id.

endpoints.name: Organization Files
endpoints.description: The files attached to one company. Requires an organization id.

endpoints.name: Organization Updates
endpoints.description: The change history of one company, with field changes and linked records. Requires an organization id.

endpoints.name: Organization Followers
endpoints.description: The users following one company. Requires an organization id.

endpoints.name: Organization Mail Messages
endpoints.description: The email correspondence linked to one company. Requires an organization id. Depends on email sync being enabled.

endpoints.name: Organization Permitted Users
endpoints.description: The users allowed to see one company. Requires an organization id.

endpoints.name: Organization People
endpoints.description: The contacts belonging to one company. Requires an organization id. The persons collection filtered by org_id.

endpoints.name: Organization Relationships
endpoints.description: The links between one company and others -- parent, subsidiary and related. Requires an organization id. Corporate structure, which the organization record itself does not express: without this a parent group and its subsidiaries look like unrelated customers.

endpoints.name: Organization Relationship
endpoints.description: One organization relationship by id, with both sides and the relationship type.

endpoints.name: Permission Sets
endpoints.description: The permission sets available on the account -- named bundles of capabilities such as admin, manager or regular user. The vocabulary that roles and users are granted from.

endpoints.name: Permission Set
endpoints.description: One permission set by id, with the capabilities it contains.

endpoints.name: Permission Set Assignments
endpoints.description: The users holding one permission set. Requires a permission set id.

endpoints.name: People
endpoints.suffix: /api/v2/persons?owner_id={Owner ID?}&filter_id={Filter ID?}&org_id={Organization ID?}&updated_since={Updated Since?:yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ}&updated_until={Updated Until?:yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ}&custom_fields={Custom Field Keys?:key1,key2,... (max 15)}&sort_by={Sort By?:id|update_time|add_time}&sort_direction={Sort Direction?:asc|desc}
endpoints.description: The contacts on the account, one row each -- what Pipedrive calls persons. Carries name, the organization and owning user, add_time and update_time, and the running counts of open, won, lost and closed deals plus done and undone activities. TWO SHAPE TRAPS. EMAILS AND PHONES ARE ARRAYS, not single values: each entry carries the value, a label such as work or home, and a primary flag, so a person with three addresses is one row with a nested list and reading 'the email' means picking the primary one. And custom fields follow the v2 rule -- returned only under the keys named in the custom_fields parameter, decoded by Person Fields. The deal counts are already computed, so per-contact value questions rarely need the deals table at all.

endpoints.name: Person Search
endpoints.description: Contacts matching a search term across name, email, phone and custom fields. Returns scored matches rather than full records.

endpoints.name: Person
endpoints.description: One contact by id. Same array-shaped emails and phones, same custom_fields rule.

endpoints.name: Person Activities
endpoints.description: The activities linked to one contact. Requires a person id. The activities collection filtered by person_id.

endpoints.name: Person Deals
endpoints.description: The deals linked to one contact. Requires a person id. The deals collection filtered by person_id, so the deal filters -- status, update-time range, custom fields -- all apply here too.

endpoints.name: Person Files
endpoints.description: The files attached to one contact. Requires a person id.

endpoints.name: Person Updates
endpoints.description: The change history of one contact: field changes with old and new values, plus linked notes, activities and files. Requires a person id. The contact record carries only its current state, so this is the only source for when it changed.

endpoints.name: Person Followers
endpoints.description: The users following one contact. Requires a person id. Internal interest.

endpoints.name: Person Mail Messages
endpoints.description: The email correspondence linked to one contact. Requires a person id. Requires email sync to be enabled; without it this is empty rather than absent, which reads as 'no contact was made'.

endpoints.name: Person Permitted Users
endpoints.description: The users allowed to see one contact. Requires a person id. Visibility configuration.

endpoints.name: Person Products
endpoints.description: The products associated with one contact. Requires a person id. Derived from the deals they are on, so it reflects what they have been quoted rather than a purchase history.

endpoints.name: Person Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a contact can carry, standard and custom, with the field key, name, field_type, and the option list for enum and set fields. THE KEY TO CONTACT DATA -- custom fields appear on persons as 40-character hashes and single-select values as option ids, neither readable without this table.

endpoints.name: Person Field
endpoints.description: One person field by id, with its options.

endpoints.name: Pipelines
endpoints.description: The sales pipelines on the account, each with name, order and whether deal probability is enabled. A pipeline is a sequence of stages, and most organisations run more than one -- so any funnel question needs to name the pipeline, or it mixes processes that are not comparable.

endpoints.name: Pipeline
endpoints.description: One pipeline by id.

endpoints.name: Pipeline Conversion Rates
endpoints.description: Stage-to-stage conversion for one pipeline over a period: how many deals moved from each stage to the next, the conversion rate at each step, and the overall won rate. Requires a pipeline id and a date range. A READY-MADE FUNNEL -- computing this from the deal records would need the full stage history out of Deal Updates, one request per deal, so this endpoint saves a great deal and is the right answer to where deals stall.

endpoints.name: Pipeline Deals
endpoints.description: The deals currently in one pipeline. Requires a pipeline id. Equivalent to filtering Deals by pipeline_id, and it can be grouped by stage in the response, which is what makes it convenient for a funnel snapshot.

endpoints.name: Pipeline Deal Movement
endpoints.description: How deals moved through one pipeline over a period: what entered each stage, what left, what was won and lost, and the average time spent per stage. Requires a pipeline id and a date range. The velocity companion to the conversion rates -- it answers how LONG a stage takes, not just how many survive it.

endpoints.name: Products
endpoints.description: The products or services the account sells, one row each. Carries name, code, unit, tax, the active and selectable flags, visibility, and the owning user. NOTE THE PRICE SHAPE: prices is an ARRAY with one entry per currency, each carrying the price, cost and overhead cost -- there is no single price column, so reading 'the price' means choosing a currency first. What was actually charged on a deal is in Deal Products, not here. Custom fields follow the v2 rule.

endpoints.name: Product Search
endpoints.description: Products matching a search term across name, code and custom fields. Returns scored matches.

endpoints.name: Product
endpoints.description: One product by id, with its full per-currency price array.

endpoints.name: Product Deals
endpoints.description: The deals a given product is attached to, with the quantity and price on each. Requires a product id. Revenue per product is built from here -- the product record itself carries a list price, not what was actually sold.

endpoints.name: Product Files
endpoints.description: The files attached to one product. Requires a product id.

endpoints.name: Product Followers
endpoints.description: The users following one product. Requires a product id.

endpoints.name: Product Permitted Users
endpoints.description: The users allowed to see one product. Requires a product id.

endpoints.name: Product Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a product can carry, standard and custom, with key, name, type and options. The decoder for hash-keyed product custom fields.

endpoints.name: Product Field
endpoints.description: One product field by id, with its options.

endpoints.name: Recent Changes
endpoints.description: Everything created or modified across the account since a given timestamp -- deals, persons, organizations, activities, notes, files, users and more in ONE feed, each row tagged with its item type. Requires a since_timestamp. This is the incremental-sync endpoint: it exists so a downstream copy can be kept current without re-reading every collection, and it is the only place a single query spans all object types. Rows of different types have different shapes, so it cannot be treated as one uniform table.

endpoints.name: Roles
endpoints.description: The roles defined on the account, with name, the parent role, and how many users and other roles sit under each. Roles nest, and a child inherits from its parent, so a permission not visible on a role may still apply through the one above it.

endpoints.name: Role
endpoints.description: One role by id, with its parent and counts.

endpoints.name: Role Assignments
endpoints.description: The users assigned to one role. Requires a role id. The membership behind a role, which the role record only counts.

endpoints.name: Sub-roles
endpoints.description: The roles nested under one role. REMOVED: absent from Pipedrive's current API description. The hierarchy is still readable from the parent_role_id column on Roles.

endpoints.name: Role Settings
endpoints.description: The permission settings of one role -- what its members may see and do. Requires a role id. Where visibility rules are actually written, and therefore the explanation for records that some users cannot see at all.

endpoints.name: Search
endpoints.description: Searches across several item types at once -- deals, persons, organizations, products and more -- for a term. Returns matches with a relevance score and an item type on each, so the result set is mixed-shape rather than one table. Reach for a specific resource's own search when the type is already known; this is for when it is not.

endpoints.name: Field Search
endpoints.description: Searches ONE named field of one entity type for a term, returning the matching values. Built for autocomplete, so it returns field values rather than whole records. NOTE V2 RENAMED EVERY PARAMETER HERE: the entity is now entity_type, the field is field, and the old exact_match became a three-valued match of exact, beginning or middle.

endpoints.name: Stages
endpoints.description: The stages making up the pipelines, each with its name, the pipeline it belongs to, its order_nr and its deal_probability. Deals reference a stage_id, so this is the dimension any funnel breakdown joins to. NOTE the probability is a configured expectation, not a measured rate -- Pipeline Conversion Rates is where the measured one lives. Filter by pipeline_id for one pipeline's stages in order.

endpoints.name: Stage
endpoints.description: One stage by id.

endpoints.name: Stage Deals
endpoints.description: The deals currently sitting in one stage. Requires a stage id. A snapshot of the stage's contents; how deals arrived and how long they have been there comes from Pipeline Deal Movement.

endpoints.name: Teams
endpoints.description: The teams on the account, with name, manager, members and whether each is active. Teams group users for goals and reporting, so this is the dimension a per-team target is measured against. NOTE THE PATH: Pipedrive renamed this resource to legacyTeams when it introduced a newer teams feature, and the connector now points at the current name.

endpoints.name: Team
endpoints.description: One team by id, with its members.

endpoints.name: Team Users
endpoints.description: The users in one team. Requires a team id.

endpoints.name: User Teams
endpoints.description: The teams one user belongs to. Requires a user id. A user can be in several.

endpoints.name: Users
endpoints.description: The user accounts on the account, one row each, with name, email, whether each is active, their locale and timezone, created and modified times, and their role and access rights. Deals, activities and every other record carry an owner user_id, so this is the dimension all per-person performance analysis joins to. Note that deactivated users remain here with active_flag false and still own their historical records -- excluding them loses that history rather than tidying it.

endpoints.name: User Search
endpoints.description: Users matching a name or email term. The lookup route when the user id is not known.

endpoints.name: Currenct User
endpoints.description: The account the API token belongs to, with its company, locale and access rights. One record, always the caller. Worth reading first when results look short, since visibility rules filter nearly every listing by what this user may see. (The endpoint name carries a typo in the connector; the resource is the current user.)

endpoints.name: User
endpoints.description: One user by id. Same fields.

endpoints.name: Blacklisted Email Addresses
endpoints.description: Email addresses excluded from one user's mail sync. Requires a user id. REMOVED: absent from Pipedrive's current API description.

endpoints.name: User Followers
endpoints.description: The users following one user. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: User Permissions
endpoints.description: The permissions one user holds: whether they can add or delete deals, see other users' records, export data and so on. Requires a user id. The direct explanation for why one person's totals differ from another's.

endpoints.name: User Roles
endpoints.description: The roles assigned to one user. Requires a user id. Roles carry the permission settings, so this is one half of what a person can do; Role Settings is the other.

endpoints.name: User Role Settings
endpoints.description: The permission settings that apply to one user through their role. Requires a user id. The resolved answer, as opposed to the role assignment alone.

endpoints.name: User Connections
endpoints.description: The third-party accounts the calling user has connected, such as Google or Microsoft. Integration state, and what determines whether the mail and calendar tables have anything in them.

endpoints.name: Current User Settings
endpoints.description: The calling user's own settings -- display preferences, default currency, timezone. Personal configuration.

endpoints.name: Webhooks
endpoints.description: The webhooks configured on the account: the target URL, the event and object each subscribes to, and its owner. Integration configuration -- deliveries are not recorded here. Worth checking to find out whether an external system is already receiving this data in real time.
